newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: KUWAIT SEES OIL PRICE DROP IF OPEC QUOTAS BUSTED.
newsitem.headline: KUWAIT SEES OIL PRICE DROP IF OPEC QUOTAS BUSTED.

text.p: Kuwait Oil Minister Isa al-Mazeedi warned Friday that oil prices would fall over the next few months if OPEC members did not honour their commitments to stop producing above official quotas.

In a briefing for reporters the day after OPEC oil ministers agreed to hold the 11-member cartel's production ceiling at 25.03 million barrels per day (mmbpd)for another six months, Mazeedi said Kuwait and other countries had put pressure on quota-busting members, particularly Venezuela, to stop overproducing.
He said all members were asked for and gave assurances that they would stick with their allocations.

But asked if he expected oil prices to fall in coming months if production continues to exceed the ceiling, Mazeedi said: "I think so. Production should be at the ceiling. To flood the market is not the right way."

With estimates that OPEC is producing some two mmbpd above its self-imposed ceiling, Mazeedi said discussions at Wednesday's ministerial meeting were "frank and tough," with Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and United Arab Emirates (those countries sticking closest to their quotas and below their production capacities) pressing for assurances from the cheaters.

Asked if Venezuela had admitted to producing above its 2.359 million bpd ceiling, Mazeedi said: "This is not something tiny you can hide under your armpit. There is over 800,000 (bpd) overproduction. Their allocation is not 3.2 (mmbpd) it is 2.359 (mmbpd) and they have promised they are sticking with that."
As well as Venezuela, independent sources show Nigeria and Qatar as producing significantly above their OPEC allocation.
Venezuela's oil minister on Thursday denied to reporters that his country was producing above its quota.
But despite the tough talk, Mazeedi said there had been no threat of any action against the quota-busters if they continue to exceed their quotas.
